title: Care pathways and needs in complex infections with multidrug-resistant organisms following war injuries: a qualitative needs and pathway analysis
summary:
People with war injuries often develop wound infections caused by bacteria that hardly any antibiotic can still treat. Treatment is lengthy and demanding. Since 2022, such patients from Ukraine have also been treated in German hospitals, including Heidelberg University Hospital. Many different departments are involved in this care, often across several hospitals.

How this care actually takes place in Germany, and where it reaches its limits, has not yet been systematically described. As a result, there is also no basis for determining what hospitals would need to have in place if more such patients had to be cared for in the future.

In this study, individual interviews are conducted with professionals who have been involved in caring for such patients or in coordinating their care. These conversations are used to piece together how the care pathway typically unfolds, at which points decisions are difficult, and what those involved feel is missing. In addition, general figures on the course of treatment are compiled from the treatment documentation of the affected patients at Heidelberg University Hospital and analyzed in summarized form.
conditions: infections with multidrug-resistant organisms following war injuries

interventions.name:
Non-interventional, qualitative descriptive study on the care pathway and needs of patients with infections caused by multidrug-resistant organisms following war injuries.

The care pathway and needs are ascertained through single semi-structured individual interviews with medical, scientific/tech

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Interviews:
• Personal professional experience in the field of complex infections with multidrug-resistant organisms in war-injured patients or comparable crisis scenarios, consisting of involvement in care, in diagnostic or advisory co-assessment, or in scientific work on the topic; or formal organizational or strategic responsibility for the coordination of care, even without personal experience with the patient group described.
• Legal age and capacity to consent
• Professional activity in Germany and sufficient German language skills for an informed conversation

Retrospective process metrics:
All cases of war-injured patients > 18 years documented at Heidelberg University Hospital with associated infections (skin and soft tissue infections, bone, joint, foreign-body-associated, intra-abdominal, intracranial infections) who were treated at Heidelberg University Hospital since March 2022 (start of the collection period corresponding to the beginning of the Russian war of aggression against Ukraine). The number of patients is not known in advance, as the collection is conducted as a complete case ascertainment of all cases within the period. Based on the assessment of the study leadership, a case number of < 10 patients is expected. The actual number will only be determined through systematic review. The period of data to be processed extends from March 2022 to the date of data extraction.
Exclusion criteria:
Interviews:
• Neither personal professional experience as described above nor organizational or strategic responsibility as described above.
• Minor age
• Limited capacity to consent
• Insufficient German language skills for an informed conversation

Retrospective process metrics:
• Patients without an associated infection as described above (skin and soft tissue infections, bone, joint, foreign-body-associated, intra-abdominal, intracranial infections)
• Patients without documented context of a war injury
